set.tovw: Hoard recovered by the heirs 1893, $26,220; yard sifting planned
set.pl: Fagan home five miles N of Holly (Oakland County Advertiser 1893); pin on GNIS Holly, farm not yet placed
set.st: Ex-whaler brothers John (82) and Thomas (78) Fagan (Fagin) were found dead at their home five miles north of Holly on 25 Feb 1893. Money turned up in wool fleeces, kegs, clover-seed sacks and the attic; the reported total rose from $8,500 to $13,500, $14,750 and finally $26,220 with Pontiac bank certificates. A rise in the cellar floor yielded a tapering crock under a stove lid holding $3,900 in gold (latest coin 1857), and the yard was to be sifted. An early wire figure of $50,000 and a Detroit News tale of money under a Pontiac sidewalk were not borne out (the sidewalk story was called a fake). Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Recovered by the heirs in 1893: record only. The farm lay five miles N of Holly (1890s Oakland plat, Holly / Rose twps). Access: private.

src: Oakland County Advertiser (Holly), 2 Mar 1893, p. 1 'Two Misers Dead' (newspapers.com 1078874162)

tw-mi-big-beaver-harris-tin-box.st: The hider was his grandfather Benjamin Sturgis, a reputed miser (d. c.1879) who 'buried and hid money about the place'; other heirs claimed the box and 'a more thorough search of the old homestead' was promised. No later find reported.
